items.reviewer_notes: A medium-tier jumble engineered so that the expected shape (claim, mechanism, examples) is wrong and the actual shape (claim, examples, generalisation) is fixed by one phrase. Heuristic solvers who order by 'general before specific' lose here.

items.title: The Bus That Emptied No Cars
items.theme: what free public transport actually changes
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); the v2 exemplar
items.reviewer_notes: A concession-turn item where the last sentence does real work: it keeps the author from the conclusion the evidence seems to invite. Three distortion families: logic (the turn collapsed), stance (flipped to dismissal), addition (a prescription).

items.title: The Pill That Works Before It Dissolves
items.theme: why placebo effects are largest for pain, and what makes them larger still
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); the v2 exemplar
items.reviewer_notes: A medium-tier item where the outlier shares the noun, the field and a connective with the core. The item teaches that 'therefore' is not a passport: a sentence must serve the paragraph's purpose, not merely follow from its topic.

items.title: Following Without Believing
items.theme: why a valid proof can fail to persuade: the proof as certificate versus the proof as explanation, and reading for the one decisive step
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation short: problem, diagnosis, remedy in three signposted paragraphs. The detail question carries the near-tie (a single negation separates the finalist from the key); the purpose question offers the memorable distinction as a decoy for the passage's actual job.

items.title: Set Apart and Forbidden
items.theme: how the category of the sacred moved from the property of the gods to whatever a community sets apart and forbids, and whether extending it to godless societies was a discovery or a redefinition
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: A short history-of-an-idea in three stages, closing on an unresolved dispute. The EXCEPT question tests stage-tracking (which stage said what); the inference question lives on the defenders' single sentence; the main-idea question offers each stage's content as a thesis.

items.title: The Repair That Was a Move
items.theme: why reforms produce consequences their designers did not intend: a reform as a move that invites a reply, not a repair to a machine
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: An analogy-driven short: the repair versus the move, carried by the chess image and three one-line examples. The final paragraph qualifies the analogy (people are not opponents), and every question is designed to punish readers who take the vehicle of the analogy for the claim.

items.title: Register · the right word for the room
items.reviewer_notes: The first register bundle: twenty sentences whose genre, a notice, a contract, a methods section, a recipe, an obituary, a commentary, fixes which of four near-synonyms belongs. Wrong options carry the right meaning in the wrong room, the wrong colouring, the wrong strength, or a collocation the sentence refuses.

items.title: Register · the room's own verb
items.reviewer_notes: The stretch register bundle: the rooms are subtler, an academic hedge, a court's ruling, a communiqué, a forecast, a leaflet, an opinion column's escalation, and several options are formal but wrong in sense.

items.title: Connotation · the same meaning, a different colour
items.reviewer_notes: The first connotation bundle: each sentence carries an attitude in its other words, admiration, complaint, alarm, tenderness, and only one of four near-synonyms carries the same attitude. The traps are the approving word in a disapproving sentence and the reverse, plus the word at the wrong strength.

items.title: The Question the Pilot Never Asks
items.theme: why pilots succeed and rollouts fail: a pilot measures efficacy under attention while a rollout depends on a supervisory capacity that cannot be extended, so the two are different questions rather than one biased measurement
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: Two accounts of the pilot-to-scale gap are given their due and then both refused, not because they are false but because they answer the wrong question. The near-tie sits in the agreement question, where a distractor converts the author's 'not sufficient' into 'irrelevant'.

items.title: Worth Watching
items.theme: why satire fails against a figure who cannot be shamed: its force is borrowed from what the target has staked on an audience's good opinion, and what survives is an audience-facing function the author refuses to call equivalent
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: A narrative that looks like an anecdote about a spoiled joke and is really about where a joke's force comes from. The set punishes the two easy readings: that the sketch was at fault, and that the closing paragraph is a consolation.

items.title: What Travels and What Does Not
items.theme: food prohibitions versus food procedures as boundary markers: the first is kept alone and portable, the second requires co-performers, so dispersal dissolves a shared practice into a stated identity without anyone abandoning anything
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: A contrast passage whose two terms are easy to state and hard to keep apart under pressure. The set turns on cost: abstention is paid by one person, coordination by a group, and almost every distractor is built by forgetting which is which.

items.title: The Sentence You Cannot Finish
items.theme: whether language shapes thought: obligatory grammatical marking as a habit of attention built by repetition, replacing the picture of a grammar that walls off what its speakers can think
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation-level passage on a topic usually written badly. The familiar strong claim is stated and refused in the second paragraph, so every question is really a test of whether the reader kept the refusal. No named languages and no trivia: the illustration is hypothetical on purpose.

items.title: Good Form
items.theme: manners as moral practice rather than decoration: a manner claims nothing about feeling, which is why it can make consideration reliable, and why an arbitrary code can still be judged by whether it puts a stranger at ease
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: Two objections are conceded at length before the turn, so the passage reads for two paragraphs as an attack on its own thesis. The set is built to catch readers who stop at either concession, and the scope question checks whether the reader kept the narrowed version at the end.

items.title: Nine Times in Ten
items.theme: explaining a belief versus justifying it: why the causal question is asked only after the verdict, and the single condition under which a causal story really does bear on a belief's standing
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: A claim, then a carefully drawn exception. The whole set turns on one substitution the passage anticipates and refuses: readers who take the qualification to be about the believer's motive rather than about the process will pick the wrong option three times out of four.

items.title: Due for a Change
items.theme: the gambler's fallacy and the expectation of a streak as one habit meeting two assumptions about the source, and why only one of the pair is an invalid inference
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-01
items.reviewer_notes: The hardest item in the batch. Everything depends on which assumption about the source yields which expectation, and the two are easy to swap under time pressure; the application question is built to punish exactly that swap. The final paragraph breaks the symmetry the rest of the passage has been building, which is where the agreement question lives.

items.title: The Hour That Was Never Enough
items.theme: why our estimates of how long work will take stay wrong however often they are corrected
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation-tier jumble with no engineered trap: one general claim, one case, one explanation and one closing qualification, each carrying a plain signal. It exists to teach the two habits the harder items assume: open with the sentence that needs nothing before it, and let explicit connectives place the rest.

items.title: The Empty Wall Beside the Picture
items.theme: why the bare wall a gallery leaves around a painting is part of how the painting is seen
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation-tier argumentative jumble whose only difficulty is a repeated noun. 'Wall' appears in the first and last sentences of the correct order, which invites a solver to glue them; the connectives override the repetition. Written to teach that a shared word is a hypothesis, not a link.

items.title: The Numbers Nobody Would Allow
items.theme: how quantities less than nothing were used for two centuries before they were admitted to exist
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced chronological jumble built on one weaponised connective. The 'Yet' sentence shares its vocabulary with the opening sentence and looks glued to it; the relative clause inside it names a denial that only the second sentence makes, so the pair must be separated. A surface solver who follows repeated words gets this item wrong.

items.title: The Map Made of Smells
items.theme: the evidence that ocean-going seabirds find their way home partly by scent
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An easy claim-and-evidence jumble whose tail is locked by one demonstrative. No trap is engineered, but a mild lexical decoy joins the opening claim to the sentence about open water; the demonstrative in the final sentence settles the order regardless.

items.title: The Biscuit and the Reach of Fleets
items.theme: how the keeping qualities of food and water, not doctrine, set the limits of naval power
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A ninety-nine tier five-sentence jumble whose difficulty is concentrated at the tail: three candidate endings, separated only by a 'therefore', a definite phrase and a demonstrative. The opening is also contested, since the sentence about biscuit begins with a bare noun and only a possessive pronoun betrays its dependence.

items.title: The Explanation Nobody Can Check
items.theme: whether a right to be told why an automated decision went against you is worth anything without the means to contest the answer
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A premium four-sentence jumble in which the false join is made by a repeated noun across a question and a finding, and broken by a demonstrative inside the finding. The paragraph is abstract throughout and offers no chronology or example to fall back on, so the solver must work purely from reference.

items.title: The Judgement That Could Not Be Inherited
items.theme: why an organisation built on one person's good judgement fails after that person leaves, and what can be done about it in advance
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-plus problem-and-solution jumble whose trap is placed at the head rather than the tail. The decoy opener has every surface property solvers look for in a first sentence and two definite references that disqualify it; the real opener is the least quotable sentence in the set.

items.title: The Street That Keeps You Interested
items.theme: the hypothesis that a street's pleasantness depends on how often it gives the walker something to notice, rather than on its beauty
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A premium hypothesis-and-support jumble locked by a measurement rather than by a connective. The two supporting sentences are parallel cases that must run in one direction only, because the second borrows its length from the first; the closing inference is marked as an inference by a single modal.

items.title: The Quiz That Teaches
items.theme: why recalling material is a better way to learn it than reading it again, and why the effort is the point
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier jumble that teaches the anchor-pair defence in its mildest form. Two sentences share the vocabulary of retrieval and look inseparable; the tail is settled by one definite phrase. Written so that a solver who reads for reference rather than for repetition gets it quickly.

items.title: The Cost of Making a Deal
items.theme: why so much economic activity is organised by instruction inside firms rather than by prices in a market
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-plus jumble built on definite articles. Three sentences open with the, the claim, the reason, and a demonstrative pointing at costs, and each points at a different antecedent. The decoy is a pair of sentences that share the vocabulary of markets and prices while answering different questions.

items.title: Register · four formal words, one formal room
items.reviewer_notes: The elite register bundle. Unlike the core and stretch sets, slang is almost never the answer's rival: in every item all four options are educated, formal words, and the discrimination is which professional room wrote the sentence, a judgment, a minute, a statute, a referee's report, a policy, a will. Three rivals per item fail on a locatable ground: the verb takes the wrong object, the act named is a different act, or the word imports a feeling the genre does not express.

items.title: Connotation · the colour the sentence has already chosen
items.reviewer_notes: The second connotation bundle, a band harder than the core set. Each sentence contains its own verdict, a consequence, a clause of concession, a gloss after a colon, an explicit denial, and the four options share a denotation while differing in what they think of it. The rivals are not slang: they are respectable words whose approval, disapproval, intensity or scope the sentence has already excluded.

items.title: Only One Thing at a Time
items.theme: counterfactual history as a disciplined method: every causal claim already contains a counterfactual, the discipline is a minimal rewrite and a short chain, and what a good one establishes is contingency rather than an alternative past
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: A definition-then-application passage where the two conditions stated in the second paragraph decide four of the five questions. The near-tie sits in the inference question, where a narrow vote satisfies the first condition and a reader is invited to treat that as enough to settle what the alternative would have produced.

items.title: The Second Judgement
items.theme: applying trial evidence to an individual patient: the average is an estimate for whoever resembles the enrolled, so the real judgement is about resemblance, and an unnamed difference is not a reason to depart from the result
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: The passage refuses both familiar positions, which is what the relationship and agreement questions are built on. The fourth paragraph rejects the sceptic and the fifth refuses to let the manualist collect the winnings, and readers who stop after the fourth carry away half the argument.

items.title: A Multiplier, Not a Gift
items.theme: the rule of law as a formal virtue whose worth is conditional: predictability makes usable whatever room the law's content leaves, so it multiplies liberty rather than supplying it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: Three short paragraphs, three positions, and a thesis that arrives only in the last four sentences. The formal account stated in the opening paragraph survives into the author's view, which is what makes it the strongest wrong answer to the main-idea question.

items.title: The Tools That Happened to Fit
items.theme: why mathematics invented for its own sake so often fits the physical world: most of it never fits, physicists go looking for the parts that do, and a small residue of exact prediction survives the explanation
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item: plain sentences, one claim, two supports and a short concession. The only real work is keeping the concession of the third paragraph out of the author's case, which is what the EXCEPT question tests.

items.title: Finding, Not Finding Out
items.theme: intent in criminal law as an imputation made from conduct by standing presumptions, which answers the objection that mental states cannot be observed but narrows the difference the traditional defence of intent relies on
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: The adjudication in the third paragraph rescues one side and then charges it for the rescue in the fourth, so options that make the author a defender of the mental element are attractive throughout. The weaken question's rival restates the author's own qualification about displacement and supplies no frequency, which is the element the key adds.

items.title: The True Thing He Said
items.theme: lying against misleading: the defence that the hearer completes the inference fails once the sentence was chosen for that inference, and what survives is a difference in what the deceiver has staked, which matters where the standing of assertion needs protecting
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: The hardest item of the batch. The passage destroys one defence of a distinction and then rebuilds a narrower one on a different footing, so every question turns on which of the two differences an option is talking about: the contribution to the false belief, which the author denies differs, or the exposure, which he says does.

items.title: Judged Against a Memory
items.theme: why cuisines change so much more slowly than dress: a dish is judged against a remembered version and sits inside a tuned system, so departure reads as error rather than novelty until circumstances remove the choosing
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: A short passage with two mechanisms and a closing pivot that turns the whole account round. The pivot is what makes sentiment the wrong answer everywhere in the set, and the word in the last clause carries two opposed senses, only one of which the sentence can take.

items.title: A Good Test in the Wrong Room
items.theme: why a highly accurate test can still be mostly wrong: accuracy belongs to the instrument while the worth of a positive result belongs to the instrument together with the population, so the same test changes value when it changes room
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: The arithmetic is given in words so that no calculation is required, and every question is decided by the third paragraph's separation of two quantities rather than by the numbers. The near-tie is in the inference question, where improving the test is offered as the remedy for a problem the test is not causing.

items.title: The Test of Saying So
items.theme: the ethics of nudging: the complaint about influence proves too much because no arrangement is neutral, so the objection should be narrowed to influence that works only while the chooser is unaware of it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: A long passage written at foundation difficulty: short sentences, concrete examples, a signposted five-step argument. The work is in the last paragraph, which limits the test the fourth paragraph has just proposed, and which most of the harder options are built to catch readers who stopped before it.

items.title: What the Reader Knows Yet
items.theme: the order of telling as a choice rather than an ornament: order fixes what a reader knows when each event arrives, so it decides which questions are available, without any order being better than another
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-02
items.reviewer_notes: A concession-then-thesis passage where the concession is unusually firm: rearrangement is refused any credit at all, twice. That is what makes every option ranking one order above another wrong, and it is the commonest thing a reader supplies for himself.

items.title: The Prize for Guessing Highest
items.theme: why the winner of an auction for an unknown quantity is systematically the bidder who overestimated it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier jumble built around a single decoy opener. The sentence a heuristic solver will place first is the third sentence of the paragraph, and the only thing that refuses it is a two-word ordinal deep inside a clause. Lexical repetition also misleads: the opening advice and the closing discipline share the vocabulary of bidding.

items.title: What the Courts Did When God Stopped Answering
items.theme: how a prohibition on clerical participation in the ordeal forced English courts to improvise a lay method of deciding facts
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-plus chronology whose difficulty is a shared noun. Two sentences end on the word verdict and invite a solver to weld them; a third sentence has to stand between them, and the only evidence for that is a reported absence. The date sentence is also a decoy opener.

items.title: The Engineer With Four Legs
items.theme: why returning beavers to a valley slows water as effectively as concrete flood defences
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A beginner item that teaches one move: find the owner of a pronoun. The surface signals all point the right way, so a careful reader who checks references will solve it directly; the only decoy is that engineers also build dams.

items.title: The Tune That Stopped Changing
items.theme: how writing a living practice down rescues one version of it and quietly ends the variation that produced it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A medium item in which the only hard evidence is arithmetic. A dozen becomes one plus eleven, and the two references to eleven fix the last two sentences absolutely. The 'Yet' is a decoy: it marks a contrast with an outcome, not with the opening scene.

items.title: Ninety-Nine Times in a Hundred
items.theme: why an accurate screening test returns mostly false alarms when the condition it looks for is rare
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier question-and-answer jumble whose tail is the contest. The illustration is written to be quotable so that it attracts the final seat, and the real closer is anchored to it by a figure the illustration alone produces. The imperative opening of the illustration also blocks it from the second seat.

items.title: One Voice From Each Side
items.theme: why a convention designed to keep reporters out of a dispute misreports the shape of the dispute, and the cheap repair
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A premium item built on one pronoun with two honest owners. Both candidate antecedents are plural, both are people, and the surrounding clause fits either reading; the tie is broken by a definite noun several words later. A heuristic solver following the nearest plural gets the second seat wrong and never recovers.

items.title: The Voice That Belongs to Neither
items.theme: the proposal that unmarked narration in a character's own idiom is what let the novel judge and sympathise at once
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier hypothesis-support item whose trap is the macro pattern itself. Solvers taught that such paragraphs open on the hypothesis will place the second sentence first; the only evidence against them is a demonstrative. The specimen line is anchored in the final seat by a demonstrative of its own.

items.title: The Line Nature Does Not Draw
items.theme: why concepts without edges force institutions to supply boundaries that can be reasonable but never correct
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A medium item with two sentences that sound like verdicts. The separation is done by a definite description that repeats the content of the sentence it depends on, which is the cleanest kind of evidence a jumble can carry and worth drilling at this tier.

items.title: Having, and Being Allowed
items.theme: the replacement of ownership by revocable permission, and why the least glamorous cases are the ones that show it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A premium five-sentence item whose whole difficulty is a false weld. Two parallel examples invite a solver to treat them as a unit, and the sentence that must sit between them is written to read perfectly well as a closing generalisation. The evidence against the weld is a superlative repeated across the two sentences it separates.

items.title: What a Price Can Take Away
items.theme: why paying people for something they were doing freely can reduce how much of it gets done
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A beginner item that introduces the definite article as a trap. Two sentences use the vocabulary of payment, and the definite noun phrase attaches to the later one; a single indefinite noun, a donation, is what proves it. Kept short and plain so the lesson is the reference, not the reading.

items.title: The Floor That Changed Places
items.theme: how the passenger lift turned the top of a building from the cheapest address into the dearest
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier chronology with one decoy opener. The lift sentence is the most interesting thing in the set and looks independent, and a single definite noun refuses it. A mild lexical decoy links the attic to the shed on the roof.

items.title: The Relatives Who Must Be Rude
items.theme: why compulsory mockery is licensed between exactly those kin whose cooperation is obligatory and whose interests collide
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier claim-and-evidence item in which one word, insult, appears at the start and at the end and invites a weld. The evidence sentence has to sit between them, and the proof is a definite description in the closer that only the evidence can satisfy.

items.title: The Words Too Common to Tidy
items.theme: why the verbs that resist regular endings are almost always the ones speakers use every day
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An easy item that teaches one high-value move: a presupposing noun beats a connective. Survivors cannot be counted until a loss has been reported, and that single word settles a seat that the But would otherwise win.

items.title: A Name for What They Were Doing
items.theme: why a word for the practitioner of science had to be coined, and what the coinage recorded about an older description
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier question-and-answer item whose concrete sentence is deliberately the most attractive closer. Two definite nouns in the real closer take their referents from it, which is the evidence that settles the tail. The paired time adverbs fix the middle.

items.title: The Help That Nobody Claims
items.theme: why money offered to poor households goes uncollected, and why the cheapest reform is a shorter form
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A beginner problem-and-solution item built on one very reliable device: a counting phrase. The list has to precede the sentence that counts it, and the surface signals all agree with the meaning, so a careful reader solves it directly.

items.title: The One Who Did Nothing
items.theme: the proposal that our lighter judgement of omissions tracks the ease of identifying an agent rather than the gravity of the wrong
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-plus item that sets two ordinals against each other. The scene offers a first and a second person; the question offers a first and a second explanation; and the sentence that says 'The second' names which kind it means only in the noun that follows it. Solvers who bind on the nearer pair lose the whole chain.

items.title: The Vote You Cannot Prove
items.theme: the secret ballot as a freedom protected by making evidence impossible rather than by forbidding pressure
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A ninety-nine tier five-sentence item in which two sentences are abstract maxims and either could open. The tie is broken by a clause at the end of one of them, which is the pattern this tier should drill. The tail is anchored by a counting phrase, so the contest is concentrated at the head.

items.title: Three Digits at a Time
items.theme: why grouping raises how much can be held in mind without the store itself growing
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A beginner general-to-specific item. The example is written so that it borrows a phrase from the sentence before it, which is the cleanest way to teach that an illustration follows the claim it illustrates rather than the topic it shares words with.

items.title: The Word That Needs a Sentence
items.theme: the untranslatable word as a claim that has shrunk: it began as a claim about what speakers could think, retreated under testing to a claim about what one word can carry, and now records only how many words a rendering takes, so what is lost is form rather than meaning
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: An easy passage whose difficulty is entirely chronological: three stages of one claim, each weaker than the last, and a closing concession that keeps a real loss in the picture. Every question is decided by which stage an option belongs to, which is why the discarded first stage is offered back three times.

items.title: Heard and Discounted
items.theme: two audience failures that are routinely confused: one is an omission that exposure repairs, the other an account of the opposition that exposure feeds, and what marks the second is not isolation but a discount fixed in advance that nothing the discounted source does can move
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: Three hundred words carrying a distinction, a consequence and a qualification that takes most of the third paragraph. The qualification is the hard part: the passage refuses to make discounting a source a fault, so every option that treats scepticism itself as the failing is out, and the deciding property is whether the discount can be moved by evidence.

items.title: The Coin, Not the Laboratory
items.theme: what makes a controlled experiment able to show a cause is the unrelated sorting rather than the laboratory, so events in the world can do the same work, at the price of having to argue that the sorting was unrelated instead of knowing it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: A long passage written at foundation level: short sentences, everyday words, an explicitly signposted view-critique-replacement shape and a fifth paragraph that states the cost in three parallel suppositions. The difficulty that remains is entirely one of holding the replacement's condition, that the sorting must owe nothing to the outcome, which every question tests from a different side.

items.title: The Pasture Without Neighbours
items.theme: the shared-pasture parable as an idealisation on the model of a frictionless plane: its inevitability is manufactured by what was removed to build it, so it forecasts well only where those removals are real, and the error is treating a result got by subtraction as a law
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: The analogy with a frictionless plane is not decoration; it supplies the passage's whole standard of judgement, which is why the structure question is answerable only by a reader who noticed that the physics paragraph is an argument rather than an illustration. The fourth paragraph then refuses to reject the model, which is what makes the wholesale-dismissal option in the main-idea question the natural mistake.

items.title: What the Room Is For
items.theme: meetings judged by information transfer, the one thing they do worst: borrowing the anthropological sense of ritual to show that a meeting distributes responsibility before witnesses, while insisting that naming a function settles nothing about whether a particular meeting is worth its cost
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: A definition is borrowed, applied to three familiar complaints, and then explicitly refused the status of a defence. The fourth paragraph is the whole difficulty of the set: readers who have enjoyed the reframing read it as decoration and answer four of the five questions as though the passage were defending meetings.

items.title: Two Cousins and a Bottle
items.theme: the paired case built to test doing against allowing removes the competing claims that make the two duties different in kind, so its verdict describes the case rather than the distinction, and the author refuses to convert that into a defence of the distinction
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: The passage answers its own opening question by attacking a method rather than a verdict, and the final paragraph refuses the conclusion most readers will already have drawn. Every question in the set is decided by that refusal, which is why the option converting the rationing point into a verdict about guilt is the live rival throughout.

items.title: What the Certificate Records
items.theme: whether a qualification adds a capacity or reveals one: the two accounts make the same predictions about earnings, so the evidence the dispute is usually fought with cannot decide it, and only cases where certificate and course come apart can
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: Three hundred words with three voices and a turn in the last paragraph that is about evidence rather than about the two accounts. The set's difficulty is that the author endorses neither side, so every option that adopts one of them is wrong however faithfully it reports it.

items.title: A List and a Reason
items.theme: prohibitions explained by what will not fit a community's scheme of kinds rather than by danger, supported by rules on people in transition and by how prohibitions end, and limited by the author's own warning that the account works only where the scheme is established before the list
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: A thesis with three supports of different kinds and a final paragraph that turns on the thesis itself. The discarded hygiene account is stated generously in the first paragraph and is then available as a wrong answer in four of the six questions, which is the point of stating it so well.

items.title: The Wars That Did Not Come
items.theme: two explanations of the absence of war between the strongest states, one about price and one about what counts as a reason, adjudicated as answers to different questions, with the relative weight of the two left as a quantity the record does not contain
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: The adjudication is unusual: the author declines to rank the two accounts and instead assigns each a different question, which is a verdict rather than a shrug. The distractors are built from readers who expect a winner, since a division of labour reads as indecision until the fourth paragraph's two clauses are compared.

items.title: Not Quite the One You Wanted
items.theme: the cycle of imitation and flight assumes a mark that can be bought exactly; a mark whose price is accumulated cannot be completed by a copier, so it is never abandoned, the test moves from possession to manner, and its holders can deny sincerely that any marking occurs
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-03
items.reviewer_notes: A scene followed by five paragraphs of reflection, with the crucial work done by the fifth and sixth: the fifth says such marks look like nothing but taste from the inside, and the sixth refuses to call the connoisseur a hypocrite. Readers who want a denunciation supply one, which is what four of the five questions are built to catch.

items.title: A Border Needs a Border
items.theme: imperial overreach explained by the argument that authorises an advance rather than by appetite: a case made on revenue carries its own arithmetic brake, while a case made on the safety of the frontier is renewed by every frontier it creates, so the expansions that ruined empires were characteristically the defensive ones, except where a frontier rests on ground nobody crosses
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: A contrast between two justifications rather than between two empires, which is where readers go wrong: they look for a comparison of places. The final paragraph attaches a condition to the contrast, and the inference question is built on that condition rather than on the contrast itself.

items.title: The Copy That Must Be Made Again
items.theme: why a medium that copies perfectly preserves worst: what fails is the apparatus that interprets a file rather than the material it sits on, so preservation becomes a recurring decision taken by whoever is currently employed, which ends the old property that neglect was survivable, while the author refuses to call the change a net loss and locates the remedy in institutional continuity rather than in any medium
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: The opening comparison is deliberately unfair and the author says so, which sets up the final paragraph's refusal to deliver the verdict the opening invites. Four of the five questions are decided by holding the fifth paragraph against the first, and the attitude question is built on the concession about completeness, which is the passage's most quotable sentence and belongs to the other side of the ledger.

items.title: The Choice Before the Accident
items.theme: liability without fault defended as a relocation rather than an abandonment of fault: the objection assumes the defendant chose only on the day of the accident, whereas he chose to carry on the activity, so the doctrine holds only where that earlier choice was declinable, unusual and to his own advantage, and the test should be the availability of an alternative rather than the danger of the activity
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: A defence that carries its own limit, so that the third paragraph is worth as many questions as the second. The doctrine is defended and then handed back to its critics for a whole class of cases, and the questions are built on readers who take the defence without the conditions or the conditions without the defence.

items.title: Bright and Empty
items.theme: the features that make a street feel safe are drawn up from the position of a frightened walker alone at night and stand in for the company that actually deters harm, while the sources of that company are the untidy small frontages such clearing removes, though reassurance still earns its place indirectly by keeping people on the pavement wherever there is an errand to bring them out
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: The concession in the opening paragraph is not a formality: the last paragraph needs it, because the thesis would otherwise be the simple inversion that reassurance is worthless. Every question in the set is decided by holding the concession and the thesis at once, and the strengthen question isolates the presence mechanism by holding lighting constant.

items.title: A Bounty on the Evidence
items.theme: a thinly sourced parable about a bounty that bred the pest it was meant to remove, widened in popular use until it names any disappointing policy, and worth keeping only in the narrow form economists gave it, where the failure requires a reward paid on a token the collector can manufacture, a condition an administrator can test before signing rather than after failing
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: The passage attacks a story's provenance in its first paragraph and then refuses to let that attack damage the idea, which is the move most readers fail to follow. Two questions are built on that refusal. The tone is the other difficulty: the author is amused by the phrase's career and severe about the claim, and options that make him either scornful or neutral are both available.

items.title: Everybody's Prudence
items.theme: a decision that raises one household's savings can lower the savings of all households together, because one household's outlay is another's receipts, but the result holds only where production is limited by willingness to buy and is a claim about the level at which a description is true rather than a verdict on thrift
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: Two qualifications in succession, one about conditions and one about what kind of claim this is, and the second is the one readers lose. The passage takes care never to disapprove of saving, which makes every moralising option refutable by a sentence rather than by a general impression.

items.title: As If It Were True
items.theme: the charge that legal fictions are dishonest misses because a fiction issues an instruction rather than a proposition, and what they actually do is import a settled apparatus of rules at the price of a sentence, whose real cost is that the moment of decision is hidden, so the objection is constitutional rather than moral and bites only where the extension is one somebody would have contested
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: A view is stated, refused, replaced, priced and then bounded, one paragraph each, so paragraph function and scope can both be asked without overlapping. The hardest thing in the passage is that the author agrees with the reformers' instinct while rejecting their reason, which makes both the dismissive and the deceived readings available for the tone question.

items.title: The Mint and the Museum
items.theme: a museum understood on the model of a mint, as an institution that certifies rather than discovers value, with the analogy pressed through several tests and then broken at one joint, since a museum's authority is reputational and revocable by the public it certifies to, which is what explains why selling a work is a scandal and melting a coin is routine
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: An analogy that is proposed, tested and then deliberately broken, with the break carrying the payoff. Readers who treat the third paragraph as a retreat lose the whole argument, and the characterisation question is built on exactly that misreading. The assumption question tests the load-bearing premise of the first paragraph rather than anything in the comparison itself.

items.title: A Mood Repaired Now
items.theme: putting things off redefined as the removal of an unpleasant feeling produced by approaching a task rather than as a misjudgement of time, a definition defended by what it predicts about which tasks are delayed and which remedies work, and qualified by the observation that the delayer is not ignorant of the cost but is arranging not to feel it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: Under three hundred words carrying a definition, three predictions and a qualification that turns the whole thing round. The last two sentences are the hardest part: the delayer is credited with full knowledge of the cost, which removes the obvious reading that he has miscalculated, and every question in the set can be decided from them.

items.title: The Warrant to Act
items.theme: the demand for evidence that a policy works is three demands, that the effect is real, that it will be reproduced by the machinery available here, and that the result is the one wanted, of which only the first is answered by trials and the third is not an evidential question at all, so the characteristic misuse of the phrase is to close a disagreement about objectives with a demonstration of effects
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-04
items.reviewer_notes: Heavily signposted, which is what keeps a long passage at this stage: first, second and third are named and kept in order. The difficulty is entirely in not letting the three merge, and four of the five questions are decided by sorting a statement into the right one of the three. The closing paragraph is a concession, and the role-of-detail question is built on readers who take it for a change of position.

items.title: Who Was Free on Tuesday
items.theme: what attendance at a public consultation actually measures
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy item whose difficulty is entirely in the fourth sentence, which refuses the inference the evidence invites. Three distortion families: scope (the mechanism widened past what it explains), stance (a description turned into a discount), addition (a remedy imported).

items.title: The Errors That Never Complained
items.theme: why a reversal rate on appealed moderation decisions cannot measure accuracy
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: The item turns on the difference between 'this number cannot show X' and 'not-X'. Three distortion families: structure (a step in the analysis promoted to the claim), addition (the implication the author declines to draw), stance (a motive imputed to the publishers).

items.title: The Fires That Were Not Allowed
items.theme: why a century of extinguishing small forest fires produced larger ones
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A causal story that invites a verdict the author withholds. Three distortion families: stance (the correction turned into a condemnation), scope (the generalisation stripped of its condition), addition (a management prescription imported).

items.title: Twenty Minutes and a Parking Space
items.theme: what closing a shopping street to traffic changes about the trade it can hold
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A concession-turn item where the thesis arrives fully qualified and the strongest distractor keeps the condition but changes the mood to imperative. Three distortion families: structure (the concession read as the point), certainty (the hedge stripped), addition (a recommendation the author never makes).

items.title: The Favour Nobody Asked For
items.theme: why people ask for help less often than they would be granted it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: The thesis is stated plainly in the fourth sentence and buried between two more quotable ones. Three distortion families: structure (half the mechanism promoted), scope (the claim recast as a trait), addition (the closing observation extended into a prediction).

items.title: The Discount and the Verdict
items.theme: what a rising rate of guilty pleas actually measures
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An elite item built on one inference too many. The near miss keeps the whole causal chain and adds the conclusion the last sentence refuses; the separating element is the difference between what a statistic measures and what it proves. Families: precision, addition, structure.

items.title: The Price That Would Not Fall
items.theme: why prices fall less than expected in a downturn, and how far the evidence settles it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An adjudication that reaches a verdict and grades it in the same sentence. Three distortion families: certainty (the verdict hardened), structure (the caveat promoted over the verdict), stance (the rejected view adopted as the author's).

items.title: The Harm That Looked Like the Illness
items.theme: why a medical practice is corrected faster when its harm announces itself
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A plain claim wrapped around a memorable example, written for the habit of matching ideas rather than vocabulary. Three distortion families: structure (the example promoted), stance (negligence imputed), scope (the claim widened to all practice change).

items.title: The Detail He Asked Not To Be Sent
items.theme: when ignorance stops excusing: ignorance that was arranged rather than suffered
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An elite item whose near miss is the textbook version of the same principle, one condition wider. The example is deliberately the most memorable sentence in the paragraph. Families: structure, addition, precision.

items.title: The Zip You Could Not Explain
items.theme: why people overrate their grasp of mechanisms but not of facts
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: The turn arrives in the fourth sentence and is carried by a calibration finding rather than by a contrast word alone. Three distortion families: logic (the turn collapsed), scope (the claim generalised past mechanisms), certainty (the hedge on 'usually' removed).

items.title: Random Against What
items.theme: what a claim that a sequence is random can and cannot assert
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: Protecting scope against the seductive stronger claim. Three distortion families: structure (the concession read as the thesis), scope (the relational claim inflated into an impossibility claim), addition (a disclosure rule the paragraph never proposes).

items.title: The Frame That Was Never Needed
items.theme: why buildings designed to be adaptable are seldom the ones adapted
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A finding whose obvious moral the author declines to draw, and says so. Three distortion families: addition (the verdict the paragraph refuses), structure (the survey result promoted over the explanation), stance (a motive imputed to designers).

items.title: The Repair Nobody Sees
items.theme: why a correction reaches a fraction of the audience the error reached
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An elite item where the near miss keeps the whole causal argument and discards a subordinate clause. Families: stance, structure, precision. The stance being protected is the author's refusal of both cynicism and futility.

items.title: The Shape and the Date
items.theme: the two accounts of the origin of the idea of progress, and what each fails to explain
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An adjudication that deliberately stops at balance. Families: stance, addition, precision. The near miss is the verdict the reader wants and the paragraph declines to reach.

items.title: The Carving Nobody Here Owns
items.theme: what the word authentic certifies in the trade in objects made for visitors
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A claim about a word, wrapped around two facts that are more memorable than it. Three distortion families: structure (the facts promoted over the claim), stance (accuracy read as deception), scope (the claim lifted out of the trade it was made about).

items.title: The Trials in the Drawer
items.theme: why averaging the published studies overstates an effect
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier item whose whole difficulty is resisting the obvious remedy. Three distortion families: addition (the reform), stance (the literature condemned), structure (the mechanism promoted over the conclusion).

items.title: The Wait at the Ford
items.theme: why settlements grew where a journey had to be broken
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item with one clear mechanism and an explicit hedge in the final clause. Three distortion families: certainty (the tendency made a law), structure (the observation without the explanation), addition (a consequence for the present day).

items.title: The White Space Between Chapters
items.theme: what the breaks between chapters do to a reader
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: The concession is generous enough to look like a thesis, and the turn is a single short sentence. Three distortion families: structure (the concession kept), scope (the claim widened to all formal division), addition (a benefit for readers invented).

items.title: The Afternoon It Went
items.theme: why a defended exchange rate can break with no change in the fundamentals
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An elite item where the example is a whole sentence and the near miss is the slogan version of the mechanism. Families: structure, precision, addition. The separating element is a range, stated twice.

items.title: The Books Beside the Book
items.theme: why commentary accumulates around a text that cannot be changed
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy item on a marked turn, where the pre-turn sentence is written to be attractive. Three distortion families: logic (the turn collapsed), scope (the condition of unalterability dropped), addition (a recommendation about how to study).

items.title: The Evening's Work
items.theme: why the argument about homework depends on the age of the pupil
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation adjudication where the resolution is a population split rather than a winner. Three distortion families: language (half the finding taken as the whole), stance (one of the two views adopted), addition (a scheduling rule).

items.title: Behind the Screen
items.theme: what a change in shortlists after screened auditions can and cannot show
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An item about the gap between an existence claim and an identification. Three distortion families: addition (the mechanism named), structure (the premise promoted), scope (the claim lifted out of auditions).

items.title: The Subscription That Replaced a Duty
items.theme: what a mutual-aid association trades away when it hires staff
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An analysis that reads as a lament until its final sentence declines to be one. Three distortion families: stance (the trade turned into a loss), structure (the benefit taken as the point), addition (a management rule imported).

items.title: The River Keeps Its Name
items.theme: why place names outlive the languages that coined them
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A clean mechanism with an explicit limit in the last clause. Three distortion families: certainty (the tendency hardened), structure (the observation without the explanation), scope (names widened to everything learned unanalysed).

items.title: Where the Knowledge Goes
items.theme: what limiting a legislator's tenure does to where expertise sits
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A concession stated at length and granted in full, then overturned without being withdrawn. Three distortion families: structure (the concession taken as the claim), stance (a relocation argument turned into opposition), addition (a comparative verdict on governance).

items.title: The Belief You Cannot Buy
items.theme: why belief cannot be adopted at will, and where a demand on a believer can fall
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A constitutive explanation that is easily swapped for a causal one, closing on a location claim that is easily swapped for a duty. Three distortion families: addition (the duty stated), structure (the illustration promoted), scope (a different kind of explanation substituted).

items.title: No Longer Late
items.theme: what happened to the shared timetable of adult life
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: Two hedges and a named alternative in the closing sentences, against a distractor that removes all three. Three distortion families: certainty (the suggestion hardened into a cause), structure (the effect reported without the conclusion), logic (the causal order reversed).

items.title: The Cost They Paid Together
items.theme: why elaborate initiation is found in some societies and absent in others
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An adjudication whose losing view remains true, which is the trap. Three distortion families: stance (the reported view adopted), language (the verdict turned into an exclusion), structure (the distributional evidence promoted over the verdict).

items.title: The Reader Who Cannot Ask
items.theme: writing defended as a technology rather than a transcription, with the usual argument from punctuation conceded to the other side and the case relocated to the one thing writing removes, the situation in which a speaker can be interrupted and can repair, so that the independence claimed is functional rather than material
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: A genuine dialectic: claim, objection, a reply that the author accepts, and then the objection restated on ground the reply cannot reach. The third paragraph is the hardest thing in the passage, because the author argues on behalf of the view he is attacking and means it, which makes both the withdrawal reading and the preparation reading available for the function question.

items.title: Out of His Own Mouth
items.theme: the printed interview explained as a device that moves the custody of a statement from the paper to a named speaker, supported by the emptiness of the early specimens and by the form of the objection made against it, and conceded the occasional disclosure that nothing else would have produced while denying that a rare outcome can account for a universal form
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: The rejected explanation is the one every reader arrives holding, so it stays available as an answer throughout. The passage's two supports are of different kinds, an absence of news and the shape of a contemporary objection, and the final paragraph concedes the rival's best case before pointing out that a rare event cannot explain a universal practice.

items.title: Worse at Everything
items.theme: why the gains-from-trade principle keeps being refused after it has been understood, adjudicated between an account that blames a mistake in arithmetic and an account that blames visible losers, with the author adding that the theorem is stated about countries and met in the form of a job, and holding that the arithmetic is not in dispute but settles nothing about the sharing
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: An easy passage by vocabulary and sentence length, with a worked numerical example, but the adjudication is real: two explanations are declared answers to different questions rather than rivals, and the author then adds a third consideration of his own. The final paragraph defends the arithmetic and refuses to let it decide a policy, which is the line the inference and implication questions are built on.

items.title: Nobody Here Knows My Father
items.theme: urban anonymity redescribed as one side of a single arrangement rather than as a service the city has failed to supply, with the freedom to release or withhold a past set against the cost borne by whoever cannot manage alone, and the remedy narrowed to forms of recognition a person can enter and also leave
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: A scene, then the received complaint given in full strength, then the same arrangement from the other side, then the cost named without softening. The two women are the passage's structural device: they are one arrangement described twice, and the temptation is to read them as cause and effect, which is what the relationship question is built on.

items.title: A Temper or a Treaty
items.theme: the paradox of tolerance handled by comparing tolerance understood as a temper, which has a quantity and no terms, with tolerance understood as a settlement, which has parties and terms, and settling for the second while denying it the comfort it appears to offer, since the obligation becomes conditional and what is owed is a standing offer answered by conduct rather than by opinion
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: Two conceptions set side by side, one preferred, and then the preferred one denied the comfort it seemed to promise. The final paragraph does three things in quick succession, prefers, concedes and limits, and the tone and inference questions are both decided there rather than in the comparison that occupies most of the passage.

items.title: Inside the Thinking
items.theme: the sense of direct access to a character's mind explained by the deletion of the reporting verb rather than by the doubling of voices, with the same deletion removing the warrant that makes an unreliable report detectable, a prediction about neutral diction offered as a test, and the word illusion restricted to its optical sense
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: The rival explanation is conceded in full and then shown to answer a different question, which keeps it live for the agreement and title questions. The hardest move is the fourth paragraph, where the same subtraction that creates the effect destroys the warrant, so the passage's most positive claim and its most uncomfortable one share a mechanism. The closing paragraph restricts the word illusion and refuses two conclusions a reader will have begun to draw.

items.title: Repeatably Wrong
items.theme: why an undisputed distinction between repeatability and closeness to the truth keeps collapsing in practice, diagnosed as an asymmetry in what an apparatus can certify about itself, illustrated by published values that moved together while their quoted intervals stayed narrow, and prescribed for by labelling which of the two a number is rather than by more careful language
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: The diagnosis is an asymmetry rather than a fault, which is what keeps the tone question hard: everything in the passage sounds like an accusation and the author twice refuses to make one. The prescription is deliberately smaller than the diagnosis, and the concession that the intervals remain worth having sits immediately before it, which is where the purpose and inference questions are decided.

items.title: The Feeling of Getting Better
items.theme: the ease of a long unbroken study session treated as evidence that the work has stopped rather than that it is going well, so that the learner's only instrument for judging progress reads the reverse of the truth, with the night before defended as well aimed at a target few people actually want
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: Plain vocabulary and short sentences, with the difficulty placed entirely in the reversal: the sensation of failure is the mechanism. The opening concession is generous and is never withdrawn, which keeps the laziness reading and the mistake reading available for the main-idea question, and the fifth paragraph refuses to compare the two methods on the morning of the test, which is what keeps the comparison question clean.

items.title: The Grass That Never Runs Out
items.theme: three successive descriptions of collaboratively written software, as a liberty, as a method and as a commons, with the third preferred for treating the practice as an institution and corrected at one point, since a resource that use cannot diminish faces desertion rather than depletion and is protected by reciprocity conditions rather than by rationing rules
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: Three descriptions in sequence, the newest endorsed and then corrected at exactly one point. The fourth paragraph is the pivot and is easy to read as a rejection, which is what the paragraph-function and scope questions are built on. The passage never says any description was abandoned, which is what the EXCEPT question turns on.

items.title: The Thing You Cannot Hand Over
items.theme: the impossibility of believing at will traced to what believing is rather than to any weakness of the will, and then confined, since attention and company are voluntary and do alter belief over time, while the indirect route only places a person where a belief may arrive, so that the looking can be demanded and the landing cannot
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-rc-003, task rc-05
items.reviewer_notes: A short conceptual argument followed by three qualifications, the third of which cuts against the first two. Readers who take the opening claim as the passage's position over-answer the characterisation question; readers who take the qualifications as a retreat under-answer it. The division between what can be asked and what cannot is stated only in the final three sentences.

items.title: The Rule That Knew Every Flood
items.theme: why a forecasting rule that reproduced every flood in its record had not thereby been tested
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A premium item built on the commonest way a general statement smuggles itself into a specific argument: by being true, quotable and on topic. The core is an accusation about one rule, and the test the learner has to run is whether any sentence uses the visitor.

items.title: The Water That Arrives Too Clean
items.theme: what happens to a river reach by reach once a dam has kept its gravel and sand
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A descriptive core whose organising principle is a route rather than an argument. The outlier is the item's most quotable fact, which is precisely why it teaches the scope test: a paragraph that is walking down one river has no position for a world total.

items.title: The Title With a Door Left Open
items.theme: what an organisation buys when it fills a post in an acting capacity rather than permanently
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The hardest regime in the set: the outlier shares every noun with the core, is locally smooth beside any of them, and is the sort of sentence a good exposition often does contain. It is excluded only by the question the four sentences are jointly answering.

items.title: The Burial That Comes Second
items.theme: why a second burial years after a death marks the end of a period served by the living
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item on the plainest stance break there is: four sentences explain what a practice does, one decides what it is worth. The decoy teaches the beginner not to exclude a sentence for having a different texture.

items.title: The Wall That Faced the Class
items.theme: how a writing surface on the front wall turned a queue of individual pupils into a class that moved together
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A narrative core with a clean chronological spine and an outlier drawn from the historian's workshop rather than from the schoolroom. The branch the mission asks for is exactly this: the story of the change, and the story of how the change was recovered.

items.title: The Apology on the First Page
items.theme: why an author can believe every sentence of a book and still believe the book contains a mistake
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier item on the cleanest tie failure there is: a comparative with nothing behind it. The decoy is deliberately the paragraph's most valuable sentence, so that a learner who eliminates by register is corrected at low cost.

items.title: The Word That Made Room
items.theme: why a word narrows its sense when a rival arrives to carry the general load
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: Two word histories, one claim. The item trains the habit of asking what an example is an example of, at a tier where the example is genuinely interesting and genuinely on topic.

items.title: The Clock That Falls Until Someone Stops It
items.theme: how a descending-price clock organises a flower market's morning around goods that cannot wait
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier item whose outlier is the sentence most readers would choose as the paragraph's opening. The core is a description with a single governing constraint, and the test is whether a general truth about auctions does any work in it.

items.title: The Note the Orchestra Waits For
items.theme: why an orchestra tunes to the oboe, and what the order of tuning records
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item that teaches the scope test with a friendly fact as the outlier. The core is short, strongly cued and closes on an interpretation, so a learner who builds first cannot miss the seat that is not there.

items.title: The Law That Has to Ask Again
items.theme: what an expiry date on a statute changes about which side inertia works for, and where the device fails
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The outlier here is built from the paragraph's own theme rather than its own topic, which is the harder camouflage: durability is what the argument is about, and the stray sentence is about durability in a department the argument never enters.

items.title: The Sentence That Went First
items.theme: how two separate conveniences at the ends of a telegraph wire settled the shape of the news paragraph
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An elite stance item where the shift is a defence rather than an attack. The core narrates causes without judging the outcome, and the outlier's calm reasonableness is exactly what makes it hard to catch.

items.title: The Price Nobody Has to Pay
items.theme: why the sums people name in a survey run above the sums they hand over, and what the named sum actually measures
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The outlier is the methods paragraph of a report standing in a paragraph of findings. It is written in the same register as the core and about the same instrument, so only the question each sentence answers separates them.

items.title: The Coat That Says Only One Thing
items.theme: why a uniform levels the people inside it and marks them to everyone outside
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier thread break with a decoy that teaches a second lesson: a conclusion may sound like advice and still be the sentence the argument was built to reach.

items.title: The Arrow at the End of the Article
items.theme: how a cross-reference let an encyclopaedia say by pointing what it could not say in a sentence
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: Two particulars, one description. The item is built so that pruning by suspicion of examples costs the learner the sentence the description depends on, while the genuine stray is the more charming of the two.

items.title: More Likely Than Not, Three Times Over
items.theme: why deciding each element of a claim on the balance of probabilities can decide the claim itself against the probabilities
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A ninety-nine item whose outlier is the most quotable sentence in the set and would open a chapter on the same subject. The core is a tight specific chain, so the uniqueness test is decisive once the learner builds before eliminating.

items.title: The Reply That Proves You Were There
items.theme: why speed of response became the visible sign of effort, and what the sign costs the work it stands for
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The outlier is the sentence a reader wants for perspective, which is why it teaches the scope habit well: the argument lives inside one working day and cannot use a statistic about a century.

items.title: The Wall That Became a Window
items.theme: how a single sheet of glass across a shop front turned goods into display and the street into an entertainment
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A narrative core with a strict causal sequence and an outlier that shares the room, the decade and the vocabulary. The only thing it does not share is a handoff, which is what the mission asks the learner to test.

items.title: Reading the Film Before You Hear It
items.theme: what a subtitle has to leave out, and what the gap does to the person watching
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier stance break in a field where opinions are plentiful, which is the point: the paragraph is explaining a constraint, and a verdict on a rival practice has no stage in that explanation.

items.title: The Liberties Somebody Was Denying
items.theme: why a town charter records what was in dispute rather than what the townsmen had achieved
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A medium-tier method break where the method sentence is genuinely useful scholarship and genuinely idle here. The argument is about interpreting a clause, and nothing in it turns on how the surviving documents are catalogued.

items.title: The Axis That Counts by Ratio
