items.title: The Line Under the Photograph
items.theme: why the claim in a published photograph lives in its caption, and why that does not make the picture decoration
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced item where the memorable half of the claim is true and the protected half is a single clause. Families: language, stance, addition. Key and one distractor both prescribe.

items.title: The First Textbook
items.theme: why the shape of a discipline is often set by whoever first had to teach it, and the condition under which that holds
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item on two limiters. Families: certainty, structure, addition. The key carries a condition, and so does one distractor, so hedging is not a tell.

items.title: The Name That Skipped a Generation
items.theme: why the revival of first names is a cycle of association rather than of novelty
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-plus item where the observation is vivid and the thesis is the last sentence. Families: structure, scope, logic. One distractor concedes and the key does not.

items.title: The Order in the Method
items.theme: why a published method should be read as an instruction for repeating a result rather than as a history of how it was found
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item whose difficulty is a refusal made in the first sentence and easy to lose. Families: structure, stance, addition. Key and one distractor both prescribe.

items.title: The Year After the Shortage
items.theme: why the worst figures in a famine district often fall in the year the grain came back, and how firmly the records support it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced item where the mechanism is strong and the author's confidence is deliberately weak. Families: certainty, structure, addition. The conceding option is the prescriptive one.

items.title: The Tic and the Contradiction
items.theme: why minor characters are given a repeatable label and major ones a contradiction, as two answers to one problem of the reader's memory
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-level item joining two observations under one function. Families: language, stance, logic. The conceding option is the one that flips the stance.

items.title: What Makes the Note Good
items.theme: how two accounts of why unbacked money is accepted divide the work between the interior of the practice and its edges
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-level adjudication that divides rather than decides. Families: structure, stance, scope. The conceding option is the one that refuses to adjudicate.

items.title: The Witness Who Already Knows
items.theme: why swearing is common where records are thin rather than where belief is strong
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item whose conclusion runs against the reader's expectation of the subject. Families: structure, stance, addition. The conceding option is the stance flip and the prescriptive one is a distractor, while the key asserts flatly.

items.title: The Clock in the Examination Hall
items.theme: what a mark from a paper that is long for its clock can and cannot be used to predict
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item on a criticism with two fences. Families: certainty, structure, addition. Key and one distractor both prescribe, and the conceding option is the prescriptive distractor.

items.title: The Frame Is Younger Than the Picture
items.theme: why a gallery's period frame is an informed guess, and why the guess is not thereby a deception
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy item where the evidence invites an accusation the author declines. Families: structure, stance, certainty. The conceding option is the stance flip.

items.title: The Rule the Neighbours Keep
items.theme: why informal enforcement redistributes the costs of order rather than softening them, and why the author will not prefer either kind
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced item where the stance is a refusal to conclude. Families: structure, stance, addition. The conceding option is the one that takes the side the author declines.

items.title: The Word That Arrived Alone
items.theme: why a borrowed word resists its new language's endings at first, and how unevenly it acquires them
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy item on four small qualifiers. Families: certainty, structure, addition. The conceding option is the one that swaps the mechanism.

items.title: The Precedent You Will Inherit
items.theme: why the restraint of a governing majority comes from the prospect of losing office rather than from the character of its members
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy item whose two support sentences are a matched pair, so the thesis is the only sentence that generalises. Families: structure, stance, addition. The conceding option is the stance flip.

items.title: What Blame Is Doing
items.theme: why the two standing accounts of blame survive each other's counter-examples, and what the author refuses to settle
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ps-003
items.reviewer_notes: An elite item whose near miss is the synthesis rather than a verdict, which is the subtler thing to refuse. Families: structure, addition, precision.

items.title: After Discussion, Agreed
items.theme: why a minute book records decisions and not the argument that produced them, and whom the omission protects
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A medium item built on one pronoun with two available antecedents, one of them wrong and nearer to hand. The decoy opener is a general hypothetical whose block sits in its final clause, so a solver who reads only sentence heads will take it. The inference marker sits in the third seat and the paragraph closes on a consequence stated as fact.

items.title: The Face You Cannot Avoid
items.theme: why a building's street elevation is the one part of a private structure that is a public matter, and what follows for the codes that govern it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A ninety-nine item whose decoy opener is stronger than the true one on every surface measure: it is generic, thesis-shaped and quotable, and the only thing against it is a remainder phrase in its second clause. The inference marker sits in the third seat and the paragraph closes on what codes actually contain rather than on a verdict about taste.

items.title: Marked Without Names
items.theme: how an examination introduced to make a candidate's connections invisible created a new thing that had to be bought
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A chronological item with a contested close. The penultimate event is the ironic one and reads like the end of the story; the true close is the sentence that names what the reform exchanged, and it is held in place by a single word about purchase. No connective appears in the final seat.

items.title: Who Does the Watching Now
items.theme: why a guarantee on deposits transfers the work of watching a bank rather than removing it, and what the uninsured reveal about the transfer
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A ninety-nine claim-and-evidence item whose trap is a pair of sentences with the same subject. The evidence belongs at the end, but it is written so that it reads perfectly well beside the mechanism it illustrates; only a counting phrase in its first three words forbids that. The inference marker sits in the second seat and the paragraph ends on the behaviour of depositors rather than on a recommendation.

items.title: Half Past Six on the Fish Stall
items.theme: why the price of a perishable good falls as the day ends, and what that shows a price to be
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A beginner item whose only real difficulty is a definite article that can be read two ways. 'The seller' looks generic and would make a serviceable opening; 'the box' in the same sentence is specific and forbids it. The paragraph closes with its general claim and carries the inference marker there rather than in the middle.

items.title: The Claim the Court Will Not Hear
items.theme: what justifies a rule of limitation that turns away claims no court has examined, and why the clock runs from when a claimant could have sued
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-plus question-and-answer item in which the decoy opener is the answer everybody already knows. Its head is a bare general statement and its tie is in the relative clause that follows. The inferential connective sits in the third seat and the paragraph closes on the design of the rule rather than on a verdict about it.

items.title: Aimed, Not Dimmed
items.theme: why the loss of a dark sky is a loss of contrast rather than of darkness, and why the remedy is the direction of a lamp rather than its quantity
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A premium five-sentence item designed so that the lexical field is useless: light appears in all five sentences. The spine is made of demonstratives and one instruction, and the decoy opener is the sentence stating the principle, whose only tie is a relative clause about a complaint. The inference marker sits in the fourth seat of five and the paragraph closes on a measured result.

items.title: Play It Again, But Not That
items.theme: why an audience will ask to hear a song twice in one evening and will never ask to hear a joke twice
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An easy hypothesis-and-support item whose single device is a contrast marker placed one seat later than habit expects. The two accounts have to arrive in order because the second is written against the first by name. The closing sentence carries the inference marker, which is the honest place for it here.

items.title: The Column That Keeps the Name
items.theme: what happens to the patients left behind when a cause is found for part of a syndrome and the name travels with the cause
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A premium five-sentence item in which one sentence is written to be both the best opener and the best closer on surface evidence, and is neither. Two small phrases settle it: 'of that kind' looking backwards and 'the negative definition' looking backwards from the sentence after it. The inference marker sits in the second seat and the paragraph ends on a fact about the literature.

items.title: The Line Underneath
items.theme: why a photograph asserts nothing until a caption does it for the photograph, and what the caption can then do to what a reader remembers seeing
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An easy general-to-specific item with no engineered device beyond given and new. Its interest is that the sentence explaining the mechanism reads like a thesis and would open the paragraph comfortably but for two words. The paragraph closes with its inference marker, which is where this argument genuinely lands.

items.title: The Line Before the First Line
items.theme: why a poem's title is part of the poem rather than a label attached to the outside of it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A beginner argumentative item whose device is a pronoun that has a plausible antecedent one sentence too early. The block is a noun in the same clause rather than the pronoun itself, which is the habit the item teaches. The inference marker sits on the closing sentence, which is where this argument lands.

items.title: When the Case Changed Its Job
items.theme: how the philosophical thought experiment moved from exposing a contradiction to eliciting a reaction, and what that licensed an objector to say
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier chronology whose decoy opener carries a date, which is the strongest surface signal of a first sentence there is. The refusal is an inversion phrase in the middle of the same sentence. A repeated phrase about the older kind of case supplies a second, purely lexical temptation.

items.title: Nobody Calls Without Warning
items.theme: why the unannounced visit disappeared without any rule against it, and who is still entitled to make one
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier item whose closing seat is genuinely contested: the verdict carries the connective and the sentimental line, and the true closer is a list. Only a three-word phrase, 'bears that out', separates them. The decoy opener is a sentence about the message everybody sends, whose definite article looks generic.

items.title: The Column Beside the Names
items.theme: why a contribution that can be read against its neighbours becomes a statement about standing rather than a gift
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-plus item whose trap is a repeated noun at the two ends of the paragraph. The envelope frames the piece, which makes the two sentences that name it look adjacent, and only a demonstrative in the final sentence forbids the join. The decoy opener is the general claim, tied down by a clause about a mechanism.

items.title: Why the Shop Is on the Corner
items.theme: why a small shop stands at a junction rather than halfway along a street, and what happens to it when the junction is closed
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A beginner question-and-answer item whose decoy opener is the answer itself, written so that it reads like a free-standing fact. The tie is in its final clause. The inference marker sits in the third seat and the paragraph ends on what happens when a junction closes.

items.title: Walking the Line With the Children
items.theme: how a society without writing keeps a land boundary by choosing witnesses who will outlive the dispute
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced problem-and-solution item whose decoy opener is a maxim. Maxims open paragraphs constantly, which is what makes the definite article inside this one easy to miss. The inference marker sits in the third seat and the paragraph closes on the custom itself rather than on a verdict about it.

items.title: The Sound of Choosing
items.theme: the hypothesis that hesitation noises mark the points where a speaker's planning is hardest, and the prediction that makes it testable
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier item in which every sentence talks about speech, so the lexical field is worthless and the two most concrete sentences are the ones a matcher will pair. The spine is a comparative, a definite article and a named prediction. The paragraph closes on what a listener is being told, with no connective in the final seat.

items.title: The Ancestor Appointed Later
items.theme: why a discipline's founding text is chosen by the field that came after it, and what the choice records about that field rather than about the past
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced item whose device is a single adverb. 'Meanwhile' marks a simultaneous story and therefore looks early, but the story it runs alongside is the book's rather than the field's, so it belongs one seat later. A possessive pronoun settles it in two words, which is the point of the item.

items.title: Written Twice
items.theme: why the schedule of exemptions rather than the operative clause carries what a policy actually does
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced item whose closing seat is contested by an instruction. Instructions feel terminal because they hand the reader a task, and this one also carries the connective; the example that must follow it is held in place by a single participial phrase. The decoy opener is that same example, which reads as a concrete first line.

items.title: The Part He Cannot Arrange
items.theme: why an apology has to be capable of being refused, and what an apology delivered before witnesses takes away from the person it names
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md)
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced argumentative item with three people in play, the offender, the wronged party and the audience, and a bare pronoun that can be bound to the wrong one. The block is not the pronoun but the clause beside it. The inference marker sits in the third seat and the paragraph closes on what the audience does rather than on a rule.

items.title: The Arm That Had to Be Built
items.theme: why the untreated arm of an experiment is a construction, and how what is put into it decides which rival explanation the comparison can exclude
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A medium-tier item whose outlier is a neighbouring question rather than a different subject. The chain is carried by three definite phrases, every such arm, those competitors, those two arms, each of which is orphaned the moment its neighbour is removed; the outlier opens with an indefinite noun phrase and is referred to by nothing.

items.title: The Marsh That Keeps Its Head Up
items.theme: how a saltmarsh raises itself by catching silt, the self-correction that keeps it level with the sea, and the one thing it needs on the landward side
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A stance item where the description is itself mildly appreciative, so the shift cannot be caught by listening for the first judgement. What marks the outlier is that it argues about money and authorities, parties the description has never introduced, while the three joints of the core are definite phrases with single antecedents.

items.title: When the Chair Speaks First
items.theme: what a chair's early statement takes out of a committee's discussion, and why the bodies that have understood it change the order of business rather than the manners
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: Written against the catalogue tell that a method versus finding outlier is simply the sentence with the numbers in it. The core carries a figure of its own, the outlier's subject is a comparison rather than a research team, and the exclusion has to be made on the chain: the shortening, the alternative to deference and the account of the interval are each unusable without their neighbour.

items.title: The Name That Moves Up a Generation
items.theme: why an adult in some societies is addressed by a child's name, and what the cases that have no child in them show the practice to be doing
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The hardest regime in the set: the outlier is locally flawless, since a consequence marker will attach to any statement whatever, and it offers exactly the kind of qualification a good argument contains. What fails is the relation. The core's own joints are a count and two definite phrases, and the argument moves from a reading offered to a reading replaced without ever passing through household size.

items.title: Paid on the Pass
items.theme: how a grant paid on examination passes changed what schools taught, and which of the two practices it produced survived the grant
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The example is placed on the very day the narrative turns on, so topic matching and even time matching approve it. What excludes it is that the story asserts nothing it could illustrate, and that the three joints of the core, the rule, the second of those two practices and the practice that ended with the grant, each lose their antecedent when a neighbour is removed.

items.title: Good to Do, Not Wrong to Omit
items.theme: why a theory that always requires the most good has no room for acts beyond duty, and why the two standard repairs close the space instead of describing it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The general sentence is deliberately orthogonal to the paragraph's claim rather than a generalisation of it, which is what stops a second four-sentence paragraph being buildable. Its camouflage is a single shared word, vocabulary, and the fact that a general opening followed by a case is a shape readers expect.

items.title: The Verb That Paid for a Tense
items.theme: why the hardening of a motion verb into a marker of the future runs one way only, and what that makes the history of a grammar a history of
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: Written against the catalogue tell that a wrong-scope outlier is simply the widest sentence in the set. The widest sentence here is a core sentence and carries the argument's only general evidence; the outlier is narrower in reach and wrong in unit, which can only be caught by asking what each sentence is a claim about.

items.title: Both Prices at Once
items.theme: what the gap between a dealer's buying and selling prices is paying for, and why the size a quote is good for is part of the price
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier item in the highest-overlap regime the tier allows: all five sentences concern one dealer quoting two prices. The exclusion rests on the question being answered, and the core's three joints are a count and two definite phrases, each of which is orphaned if its neighbour goes.

items.title: The Act Before the Corridor
items.theme: how a break invented for trimming lamps and selling drink became a rule about where an act must end, and what that makes of the symmetry now taught as dramatic form
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A premium stance item in which the core is not neutral. It judges an explanation, calling a taught property misplaced, so listening for the first opinion will not find the outlier. What marks the outlier is the kind of question it settles, worth rather than origin, and the fact that no sentence supplies it with an opponent.

items.title: The Schedule Nobody Wrote
items.theme: how separately reasonable withdrawal rates add into a rate on extra earnings that no department designed and none can see
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An advanced item built so that the method sentence is not the sentence with the most technical surface. The core's three joints, that number, the addition and the parts against the sum, are each unusable without their neighbour, and the measurement sentence is the only one nothing leans on.

items.title: The Column Left Empty
items.theme: how a narrow blank column kept for late news trained a way of opening a newspaper that outlasted the column itself
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An easy-tier thread break that does not rely on a false connective. The outlier simply joins a second sequence, in the same place and period, and is caught by asking which stage of the column's story would miss it. The core's joints are a demonstrative, a place adverb and a named habit.

items.title: Twice From Somewhere Else
items.theme: why averaging one person's two guesses helps a little, why the help shrinks when the guesses are close together, and what that turns the advice into
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The example is drawn from the same field, the same kind of person and the same task, and it fails on one joint only: the paragraph combines answers and never ranks them. The core's chain runs through the gain, that shrinkage and the instruction that follows, each of which is orphaned if its neighbour is removed.

items.title: The Rota and the Auction
items.theme: why an unpleasant shared job is distributed by a rule rather than by a bid, and what the rule is bought to keep quiet
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The general sentence is deliberately orthogonal, about membership rather than about reluctance, so it cannot be read as the paragraph's own claim stated broadly. That keeps a second four-sentence paragraph from being buildable while preserving the pull of a quotable opening.

items.title: Objections Before the Answer
items.theme: how a teaching exercise that put the objections first left its order on the page, and what that does to a reader who takes the opening for the author
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The hardest scope regime: the outlier is not the widest sentence in the set and it attaches by a demonstrative that has a genuine antecedent. Only the unit separates it, and the core's three joints, the order, that arrangement and the opening pages, are each unusable without their neighbour.

items.title: What He Saw, Not What It Meant
items.theme: why a witness is stopped from stating conclusions, and why the restriction relaxes where an observation cannot be reported without one
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item where the chain is deliberately visible: the rule, those people, the materials. The outlier is on topic but answers a neighbouring question, which is the mildest form of the violation and the right place for a learner to meet it.

items.title: One Action In, Six Out
items.theme: why the difficulty of leaving a service is a servant of the figure the organisation is judged by, and why a remedy aimed at the steps will not hold
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A stance item whose core is opinionated throughout, so the shift has to be found by asking what each verdict is about. The core's chain runs through that account, what it is scored on and the figure they protect, each of which loses its antecedent if a neighbour is removed.

items.title: A Clause Bolted to the Front
items.theme: how a building code that fixed a stair's width and reach but not its position produced a second front, and what its removal left behind
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A method sentence written in the period's own voice rather than in the voice of a modern investigator, which removes the usual texture tell. The exclusion rests on use: the narrative's four stages are caused by a clause, a silence, a price and a later code, and none of them needs a figure in a register.

items.title: Opened Now or Put Aside
items.theme: why two opposite conventions about opening a present are answers to the same risk, and what a traveller mistakes when calling one of them cold
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A thread break without a false connective. The outlier attaches by a real antecedent and simply starts a second line of development, which is the harder version of the violation to see: the reader has to notice that the line is never continued and never needed.

items.title: The List the Captain Drew
items.theme: why a regiment's pay roll cannot be corrected into a headcount, and what a historian may still take from it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: The example is drawn from the same document, the same period and the same kind of failure, and is excluded only because the defect it exhibits is not the defect the argument alleges. This is the finest version of the example that serves no claim, and the explanation states the difference in one line.

items.title: The Fifth Stroke Laid Across
items.theme: what the crossed fifth stroke of a tally adds to a row of identical marks, and what a tally kept without it loses
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A foundation item with a very strong core: three joints, the crossed stroke, counting in blocks and neither property, the last of which is a count that fails outright if either of the two benefits is removed. The general remark is orthogonal by design, about where notations travel rather than about what this one does.

items.title: Stops Go On and Never Come Off
items.theme: why an extra stop is always asked for by the people it helps and never by the people it costs, and what that does to a route over time
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A scope item in which the outlier is not the widest-sounding sentence and does carry a number, as the opening does. The break is the unit, a network rather than a route, and it is confirmed by the chain: the people whose walk is shortened, one of the two groups and the accumulation each fail without their neighbour.

items.title: The Vote Withheld in Public
items.theme: why a recorded abstention is punished more heavily than an absence although the two cost a party the same vote
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: An elite item in the highest-overlap regime available to the genre: all five sentences concern divisions, members and the people who manage them. Only the question separates them, and the core's chain runs through that absence, its readable counterpart and the two, the last of which is a count that fails if either member of the pair is removed.

items.title: The Car That Would Not Start
items.theme: why a device that made a safety habit unnecessary was refused while a device that merely asks for it was accepted, and what the replacement settled
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A medium-tier stance item whose core ends on a judgement of its own, so the shift cannot be found by looking for the first opinion. The outlier is excluded because its judgement needs a dispute the narrative never records, and because nothing before or after it uses a verdict on the legislature.

items.title: The Watcher and the Almanac
items.theme: what changed when a rule tied to a visible sign at dawn was answered by a printed table, and why some communities keep both
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: Written so that the method sentence is not the only technical one: the core carries the sharper figure, a table four minutes out, and the outlier's subject is the tables themselves. The exclusion rests on use, since no step of the exposition requires anything about how the table is produced.

items.title: The Machine With One Buyer
items.theme: why an asset useful to only one customer is often never built, and what a long contract is actually purchasing when it is written
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 (content/taxonomy/AUTHORING.md); batch-ooo-003
items.reviewer_notes: A cat-tier thread break whose false anchor is a consequence marker plus a symmetry. Pairing the buyer with the supplier looks like the natural next move in an argument that has been about one of them, which is exactly why the relation has to be tested rather than accepted.

items.title: Decline, and Pass It On

The facts follow the published account of nest-site selection (a swarm of about ten thousand, a few hundred scouts, dance repetitions scaled to quality, dances that fade on each return, a quorum of roughly fifteen at the site, piping, lift-off within about an hour). The set's near-tie is the half-right implication option that gets the timing right and the error rate backwards.

items.title: Not Her Nostalgia
items.theme: styles from about twenty years back return not through nostalgia, since the nostalgic are the people who no longer wear those clothes and the buyers are too young to remember them, but because clothes mark each age group off from the one next to it: the young avoid the styles of those just older and take up the ones no age group near theirs is wearing, which explains when a style can return though not which one will
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: A first-person foundation item: one family lunch, the usual explanation of revivals (nostalgia) refuted by asking who actually buys the revived clothes, and a replacement (clothes mark each age group off from the one next to it) with its limit stated (it explains when a style can return, not which). rc-0065 deals with imitation and flight between classes and with marks that cannot be bought; this passage is about age groups and timing, and what it adds to the familiar twenty-year rule is the observation that nostalgia belongs to the people who do not buy. One of the batch's two 'people think X; actually Y' passages (the other is rc-0122). The tone question carries the set's register; the purpose near-tie is the option crediting the author with explaining which styles return.

items.title: Fill Every Bucket
items.theme: a rumour outruns its correction because the rumour gives each person who receives it a task and a kindness to pass on, being wrong by forwarding it costs little while ignoring a true warning costs a lot, and a bare correction reports only that nothing will happen and asks the people who spread the rumour to admit they were fooled; a correction keeps pace when it is a story in its own right, such as how the mistake began, because then it too gives people something new to pass on
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal foundation item built as a puzzle explained: one morning's false warning, the mechanism that let it outrun an accurate notice (a task, a kindness, the lopsided cost of being wrong, and the embarrassment of the people best placed to correct it), and a third paragraph that limits the mechanism with a correction that did keep pace because it was a story. The familiar line that a lie outruns the truth stops at the first half; what this adds is that a correction competes on the same terms as the rumour, so a bare denial loses and a correction with news in it need not. The set's near-ties are the main-idea option that stops before 'Some corrections do keep pace, though' and the role-of-detail option that reads the old notice for its content rather than its job.

items.title: A Cup of Their Own
items.theme: tea became India's everyday drink through a campaign the tea industry began when prices abroad fell and it had more tea than buyers, but the British method the campaign taught did not catch on; the habit lasted in a form the drinkers made for themselves, boiled with milk, sugar and spice, because it tasted like the spiced milk homes already made, cost little and gave the working day a pause, so the cause that starts a habit and the cause that keeps it can be different: persuasion won the first cup and ownership kept the habit
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal foundation item told as a history: a crop grown for export, a campaign to sell it at home when prices abroad fell, and a third paragraph that turns from the persuaders to the drinkers. Facts are kept general (no organisation names, dates or figures) and no question needs outside knowledge. The usual telling is a story of successful marketing; what this adds is the distinction between the cause that started a habit and the cause that kept it, with the irony that the drink that lasted is the one the campaign never taught. The set's near-tie is the inference about the industry's point of view, where the key sets what the industry needed against what it got.

items.title: Anything on Volcanoes?
items.theme: a search can only work from the words a person brings to it, so it serves best someone who already knows what to ask; a library adds what lies outside those words, a librarian who asks what the question is for and shelves arranged by subject that put unknown books beside the one wanted, so its particular value is help before a person knows what to ask, not a larger store of facts, and for a question already known a search is quicker and just as good
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: A first-person foundation item built as a scene that becomes an argument: a boy's question at a library desk, the distinction it shows (a search works only from the words it is given; a library adds what is not in them, a librarian's question back and shelves arranged by subject), and a third paragraph that limits the claim (a library holds far less, and a search is better for a question already known). Defences of libraries usually rest on free access or quiet space; this one rests on a single mechanism, help before the question exists, and concedes everything else. The set's near-tie is the purpose option that reverses whom the library serves.

items.title: Every Hand Goes Up
items.theme: the claim that each person learns best in their own style needs more than preferences, which are real, or visual learners doing well with pictures, which most people do: it needs a crossing result, each kind of learner doing better with lessons in their own style; tests built that way have rarely found it, because whichever kind of lesson works better tends to work better for everyone, so the best form of a lesson depends on what is being taught rather than on who is learning it
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal foundation item in the 'popular idea, then what testing shows' shape, one of the batch's two passages of that kind. The learning-styles idea is well known, and the usual debunking stops at calling it a myth; what this adds is the design of a fair test (preferences and one-sided results are not enough; the results have to cross over) and a replacement principle, that the subject being taught decides a lesson's form. The claim about the evidence is kept to what it supports ('rarely appeared'). The set's near-tie is the inference option whose second half has the listeners also doing better with pictures.

items.title: Where the Grass Gives Up
items.theme: a desire path is better evidence than any survey of where walkers want to go and how far round they will go, so a planner can wait and pave the lines people wear; but the path records a destination and a budget of time, not a good route, so a track worn across a railway line calls for a footbridge in a better place, close enough to be used, rather than for paving the track
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal developing item built as a claim with its limit. The familiar campus story (wait, then pave the worn lines) is told as the lesson; what this adds is a precise statement of what the evidence is evidence of, a destination and a budget of time rather than a route, so that a track across a railway calls for a better-placed footbridge rather than paving. The fourth paragraph turns the limit into a working rule. Four questions: purpose, a one-step inference about the waiting planners, an application whose scenario mirrors the railway case, and a role-of-detail question on the concession inside the second paragraph. The set's near-tie is the application option that would pave the track.

items.title: A Long Afternoon
items.theme: boredom is useful not because it is creative in itself but because it is a signal that pushes a person to look for something better, so that the ideas come from the search; the push helps only where the person is free to act on it, so the two common reputations, boredom as an illness to cure and boredom as a gift, describe boredom one cannot and can act on, and a phone carried into free time answers the push at once, so the search that makes boredom useful never starts
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal developing item built as two views weighed rather than as a correction: both reputations survive, each with its situation marked. The creativity-from-boredom claim is familiar; what this adds is the mechanism stated exactly (boredom as a signal that pushes, so the ideas come from the search and not from the boredom), the condition on which its usefulness depends (freedom to act on the push), and the observation that the two reputations describe different situations. The fourth paragraph adds a case that fits neither view, which the weaken question targets, and the passage ends on a question. The experiment is described in general terms and no question depends on knowing it.

items.title: Mr Rao's Notebook
items.theme: a small shop survives beside a cheaper supermarket because a customer pays for the trip as well as the goods: for small, urgent purchases the trip costs more than the difference in price, so the shop is really selling a short trip, small amounts and credit, and it can give credit only because it knows its customers; so a further price cut barely threatens it, fast delivery threatens the short trip, and the credit is the hardest part for a rival to copy
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal developing item built as a puzzle explained, opening on a scene. The familiar point that a corner shop sells convenience stops at nearness; what this adds is the whole cost of a purchase (price plus trip) as the mechanism, credit as a second product that depends on knowing customers, and the consequence that a price cut barely threatens such a shop while fast delivery threatens only its first product. Four questions: main idea, a one-step inference from the condition on lending, a word in context whose trap is the notebook sense of 'copy', and an application whose near-tie is a shop that keeps the short trip but gives no credit.

items.title: Bought, Given or Taken
items.theme: the case for keeping objects taken under colonial rule answers where they are best seen and cared for, while the case for returning them answers whom they belong to; where an object was taken by force the question of ownership comes first, as no thief may keep a painting by hanging it well, so looted objects should go back, with the keeping side's worries shaping how they go back, while objects that were bought or given need their histories checked one by one, since a sale made under an occupying army may not have been free
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal developing item built as two views weighed and then decided. The restitution debate is familiar; what this adds is the adjudication: the two sides answer different questions (where objects are best kept, whom they belong to), ownership comes first for objects taken by force, the keeping side's worries become questions of how to return rather than whether, and objects bought or given are left to case-by-case history. The palace is left unnamed and described only as far as the argument needs; no question depends on outside knowledge. Four questions: purpose, a detail tied to the passage's phrase 'hard questions', attitude to the keeping case, and an application whose near-tie is a sale made under occupation.

items.title: Ending on a Warmer Note
items.theme: people judge a past experience by its most intense moment and its end because memory keeps a few moments that stand for the whole rather than a running total, so how long it lasted barely counts; the shortcut serves well for deciding whether to go back, since the most intense moment shows how good or bad things can get and the end how they stood on leaving, but it misleads when the options differ mainly in length, which is why people choose a longer trial with more pain that ends gently, and why whoever designs an experience can change how it is remembered by improving its best moment and its end
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: A second-person developing item that explains a surprising result by a mechanism and then follows a consequence. The peak-and-end finding is famous; what this adds is an account of why the shortcut is sensible (the most intense moment shows how good or bad things can get, the end shows how they stood on leaving), exactly where it fails (when options differ mainly in length), and its use by anyone who designs an experience. The passage keeps remembered pleasantness apart from felt duration, so it does not collide with rc-0116, which is about how long a wait seems. Both studies are described in general terms and no question depends on knowing them. Four questions: title, an inference about the people who chose the longer trial, the function of the third paragraph, and an application across new cases.

items.title: Sleeping on It
items.theme: a night's sleep strengthens what was learned the day before, apparently by replaying it, so that a skill can improve and a hidden pattern can surface without further practice; but sleep works only on what the day supplied, adding no new material and unable to rescue what was never properly learned, so an all-night session before an examination trades away the night that would fix the day's work for a few hours of poorly learned reading
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal developing item built as a claim with its limit. Sleep's part in memory is well known; what this adds is the limit stated as a rule (sleep works only on what the day supplied) and its two consequences, that sleep cannot add new material or rescue careless study, which turn the familiar advice against all-nighters into a conclusion rather than a slogan. It does not overlap rc-0083, which defends an evening of cramming; this passage is about giving up the night's sleep. The finger-tap and rat findings are described in general terms and no question depends on knowing them. Four questions: main idea, an inference joining the opening example to the third paragraph's rule, the role of the rats, and a weaken question whose near-tie attacks only the minor reason.

items.title: Cheaper by Water
items.theme: old cities stand on rivers less for drinking water, which villages needed too and got from wells, than because a city must bring in heavy loads of food and fuel and before railways only boats could move them cheaply, so a large inland city could grow only where boats could reach; railways, roads and pipes have closed most of that gap on land, so newer inland cities follow railways, highways and airports, but over long distances ships are still far cheaper than any alternative, so the old reason now favours ports rather than rivers
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: An impersonal developing item that sets aside the obvious answer and then follows the right one into the present. Water transport as the reason cities grew where they did is standard economic history; what this adds is the test that dismisses drinking water (villages had it and stayed small), the condition that a large city could grow only where boats could reach, and the turn that the reason has moved to the coast rather than vanished. Johannesburg and the share of trade carried by sea are stated in general terms, and no question depends on knowing them. Four questions: purpose, a detail on the cost of land transport, the role of wells and springs, and an implication from the 'only where' condition.

items.title: Plums on Trust
items.theme: people pay into an honesty box with nobody watching because cheating would cost them their picture of themselves and because they believe others pay; they stop when they come to believe that others are not paying, so a notice complaining of theft, by announcing that not paying is common, can make it more common, while a true notice that nearly everyone pays keeps the many paying, though no notice moves the few determined thieves, who need a lock
items.prompt_version: content engine v1 + CAT-size brief 2026-10
items.reviewer_notes: A first-person developing item in which a scene carries the argument. The finding behind the park signs is known; what this adds is a single case followed from cause to repair, two reasons for paying (self-image and the belief that others pay) shown to be linked, since the first weakens once the second goes, and a limit: a notice reaches the many who pay while they think others do, not the few determined thieves, so the stall ends with both a thank-you notice and a padlock. It does not overlap rc-0091, which explains obedience to law by the standing of the authority. Four questions: title, an inference from 'works only if', attitude to the first notice, and an application to a library.

items.title: Counted None the Less
items.theme: habit as a law of the body that survives the objection from sudden conversion: strong new stimuli rupture old habits by the same law rather than against it, and because the nervous system keeps whatever it is repeatedly made to do, the accumulation that makes a vice is the same one that silently builds competence

items.theme: speech feels as natural as walking but differs from it in kind: walking develops from the body in any society or none and varies only between individuals, while speech is a group's historical inheritance that varies without limit between groups, and the instinctive cries of feeling are no counter-evidence because they are not symbols

items.title: A Mechanical Purpose
items.theme: a nation, in Tagore's sense, is a people organised for power rather than a society living for its own sake: the political side of a society has a limited protective purpose, but once science and wealth let it outgrow that place it rules the society like a machine whose aim is success rather than goodness, and the charge falls on this method of organisation wherever it is used, not on any people

items.title: The Place of Formal Education
items.theme: schooling becomes necessary exactly when adult life grows too remote, in place and in meaning, for children to learn it by sharing in it, and the same remoteness is its standing danger: what is learned through symbols can stay cut off from practice and character, so that schooling turns out specialists instead of members of a common life

items.theme: a display of standing can outlast the thing it displays: as servants disappear, the duty of performing leisure and consumption on a master's behalf narrows to the wife, so that in the lower middle class a man works hard in order that his wife can be seen not to, the taste that finds her wasted effort pleasing has itself been trained to demand it, and her consumption for show survives even lower down than her leisure, reversing her role without changing her status
